criteria.no: The item gives no concrete validity assurance, or a described element is established not to execute against a supported interface.
criteria.unclear: The item addresses validity but expressly leaves an applicable element pending, or proposes a concrete element whose support or response shape remains indeterminate.
criteria.yes: The item supplies a complete supported form or requires every applicable validity element to be current and supported.

addressed.instructions: Does item.text explicitly supply or require the validity information needed for its plan-anchor examples to execute against the current repository and supported interfaces? Consider every applicable repository path, command or flag, and JSON schema or normalized envelope.

criteria.no: No actual incompatible choice is evidenced, including omission-only cases.
criteria.unclear: An actual concrete choice is evidenced but compatibility is indeterminate.

contradicted.instructions: Answer whether item.text supplies evidence of an actual incompatible example choice, not whether it fully proves executability. yes requires an affirmative incompatible choice: an invented path, removed or unsupported command/flag, unsupported JSON schema, or literal placeholder advertised as runnable. unclear requires an affirmative concrete choice whose compatibility is genuinely unknowable from the text, such as a proposed future flag with unspecified support. no applies when all concrete choices shown are supported or when the only defect is missing, postponed, or generic validity content. A missing or deferred JSON shape cannot by itself be unclear or yes for conflict. Keep contradiction independent from addressed and relevance.

criteria.no: The item is about a different part of the system or a different activity, and completing it would neither follow nor break the anchor.
criteria.unclear: The item text is too vague to tell what part of the system it touches.
criteria.yes: The item plans, changes, or depends on the thing the anchor statement is about, directly or as a clear prerequisite.

relevant.instructions: The state holds one planning item (`item.title`, `item.text`) and one anchor: a directive the user stated verbatim in `anchor.statement`, with the area it governs in `anchor.scope`. Does the work described in `item.text` touch the subject that `anchor.statement` talks about? Judge overlap of subject matter only. Do not judge whether the item obeys the anchor.
